sourceIssues.locator: Lemma 4.1, p. 12 of arXiv:2410.12560v1 and of the author manuscript (§4; journal pp. 73–94 not read)
sourceIssues.printed: Let H be a finite group, let B be a finite H-module, let F be a field, and let V be a faithful H-representation over F. For every x ∈ V^{(1)}, let H_x ⊂ H be the stabilizer of x, and choose f_x ∈ F(V)^× such that div(f_x) = x. The group (B ⊗ F(V)^×)^H is generated by (B ⊗ F^×)^H and all elements of the form N_{H/H_x}(b ⊗ f_x), for all x ∈ V^{(1)} and all b ∈ B^{H_x}.
sourceIssues.correction: The lemma needs the hypotheses under which it is applied: that B is killed by n, that e(H) divides e and that F contains a primitive root of unity of order ne. With those hypotheses the statement is correct and is what the proof of Theorem 1.3 uses.
sourceIssues.reason: Confirmed for the manuscripts. With F=R, H=C2 acting by t↦−t, B=Z/2 and x=(t), the proposed relative norm is the class of t itself, since Hx=H. Conjugation changes it by the nonsquare −1, so it is not invariant. Any square class with divisor x modulo 2 has the form ctw² and has the same obstruction. Add nB=0 and sufficient roots of unity: h(fx)/fx is a character value in μe, and μe⊂F×n makes b⊗fx Hx-invariant. Orbit generators then lift, and left exactness supplies the remaining constant term. Theorem 1.3 uses B=A(−1), n=e(A), e=e(H), precisely satisfying these added conditions; this specific defect does not refute that theorem.

sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Lemma 5.3, second and third sentences, p. 15 of arXiv:2410.12560v1 and of the author manuscript
sourceIssues.printed: Let E ⊂ GL(Ṽ ⊕ W̃) be the inverse image of GL(V) ⊂ GL(V ⊕ W). The restriction to Ṽ of any element of E belongs to GL(Ṽ). It follows that restriction to Ṽ defines a group homomorphism π: E → GL(Ṽ).
sourceIssues.correction: An element of E need not preserve Ṽ. The map π is the top-left block, g = [[A,B],[C,D]] ↦ A, and it is a homomorphism because the off-diagonal blocks B and C of any g ∈ E are divisible by p, so that all their products vanish modulo p^2.
sourceIssues.reason: Confirmed: the purported restriction map is not defined. The matrix I+pE31 reduces to the identity and lies in E, but sends e1 outside the rank-two summand. The top-left block A is invertible and defines a homomorphism because the other off-diagonal blocks are p-divisible, making their product zero modulo p². This proves the corrected diagram; the lemma itself is unchanged.
